notes: Identity checked against the supplied neutral reference: repository cover identifies Chowdhury, Jeon and Saha (2017), the exact title, Southern Economic Journal 84(2), 474–483, and DOI 10.1002/soej.12223. It labels the work Accepted Version; the manuscript title page names Subhasish M. Chowdhury, Joo Young Jeon and Bibhas Saha and is dated June 20, 2016. This is a full primary accepted manuscript with methods, results, references and instructions, not an abstract or a replication report. No PDF was supplied. Manuscript pagination is 1–16 and cannot be equated to published p. 478 without evidence. Target unresolved: every assigned description is blank and no outcome, gender, comparison or model is specified. Manuscript p. 4 Table 1 is explicitly descriptive data from Dreber et al. (2013) and Grossman and Eckel (2015), not the original experiment of this article. Own-study Table 2, manuscript p. 7, offers five Mann–Whitney comparisons: giving vs taking overall (p=0.583), males (p = 0.001), females (p = 0.039), and male vs female within giving (p=0.594) or taking (p= 0.0001). These remain distinct candidates, not assigned targets. Table 3 p. 8 offers OLS giving-game coefficients -0.004 (overall), 1.159*** (male), -1.186** (female), Female 1.097***, and interaction coefficients 2.262***, 1.155**, 1.084**; p is bounded by the printed star legend, not exact. Table 3 p. 10 instead reports Probit marginal effects for selfish/egalitarian outcomes. Footnote 6 p. 11 also reports Kolmogorov–Smirnov p-values 0.288, 0.001 and 0.039. None of these tests can be selected from row order or numeric agreement. Candidate analytic units are dictator decisions, not all 280 recruited dictators plus passive recipients. Table 2 states 70 observations per treatment overall and 35 per treatment for each gender. Potential between-frame totals are 70 + 70 = 140 overall and 35 + 35 = 70 within a gender, using mutually exclusive between-subject treatment groups; within-frame gender comparison is 35 + 35 = 70. These are candidate sums only, not extracted target N. OLS Table 3 explicitly prints 140, 140, 70, 70 observations by model. No target-specific exclusion rule is established; Probit footnote 5 describes category classification, which must not be assumed to be exclusions from another test. No Cohen’s d is printed in the inspected primary results: Table 2 gives monetary means and standard deviations plus Mann–Whitney p-values; Table 3 p. 8 gives OLS coefficients and standard errors; Table 3 p. 10 gives Probit marginal effects and standard errors. No conversion was performed. Unassigned replication and reported_success are placeholders only.
